dish: Kwak in de 1,2-liter 'Max' laars (schoen als borg) — ruim 500 Belgische bieren
w: Ghent's most famous beer café, with the city's largest Belgian-beer list (500+). Order the 1.2-litre house boot and you hand over a shoe as deposit, hoisted to the ceiling in a basket until you return the glass.

dish: huisbier Klokke Roeland; keuze uit ~175 bieren, 20 van 't vat
w: A canalside brown pub in a former riverside house with a waterfront terrace and around 175 beers, including its own Klokke Roeland. The classic Ghent beer stop, next to its jenever annex.

dish: jenever / dreupel — meer dan 200 soorten, incl. huisgemaakte fruitjenevers
w: A tiny jenever house on the water beside the Waterhuis, pouring only genever — over 200 kinds, from cactus to vanilla to chocolate — served ice-cold and brimful.

dish: Gruut Inferno & Gruut Wit — bieren gebrouwen met kruiden (gruut) i.p.v. hop
w: Annick De Splenter's city brewery revives 'gruut' — a medieval herb blend used instead of hops — in five house beers plus a rotating 'Maîtresse'. Tours and a canalside brewery bar in the centre.

dish: Gentse Tripel (in eigen huis besteld) + honderden speciaalbieren
w: A vast beer specialty shop and bar that commissions its own Gentse Tripel, alongside a huge range of Belgian and international beers, wines and spirits — the go-to for beer to take home.

dish: breed trappisten- en abdijbier-aanbod in een trollenthema
w: A characterful troll-themed beer café by Sint-Jacobs with a deep, well-kept list of trappist and abbey beers and a quiet upstairs — a beer-lover's classic away from the tourist crush.

dish: lokale bieren op twee terrassen (voorkant stad, achterkant Leie)
w: A historic pub in a former granary right in the centre, with two terraces — one on the bustling street, one over the Leie — and a solid local beer list.

dish: eigen Galgenbier in Gents kleinste bruine kroeg (sinds 1778)
w: By far the smallest café in Ghent, an 18th-century brown pub on the Groentenmarkt pouring its own Galgenbier — squeeze in upstairs or take a stool on the market.

dish: Belgische klassiekers in een 17e-eeuws bruin café (bouwjaar 1667)
w: One of the last genuine brown cafés in the centre — candlelit, chamber-pots on the ceiling, a 1667 building full of stories in the heart of Patershol. Beer and conversation, nothing else.

dish: Gentse waterzooi van hoevekip & Vlaamse stoverij
w: An authentic Patershol brasserie that does the Ghent classics properly — creamy waterzooi of farm chicken and beef stoverij braised in beer — in a warm, cosy room.

dish: Gentse stoverij & waterzooi onder de kathedraal
w: A typical Ghent brasserie in a striking black-and-white room directly below St Bavo's, with a big summer terrace on the square — the reliable address for stoverij and waterzooi in the centre.

dish: oesters & zeevruchten, Frans-Italiaanse brasseriekeuken
w: A grand belle-époque brasserie in a converted warehouse down an atmospheric alley — oysters, seafood and French-Italian classics under a soaring iron-and-glass roof.

dish: gehaktbal met vloeibare vulling (van eerlijk vlees), met stoemp
w: An open-kitchen canteen serving one thing brilliantly: handmade meatballs with a molten filling, from honestly sourced meat, with mash and greens. Walk-in, no reservations.

dish: brasserie aan het water in de oude vismarkt
w: A brasserie set in the Baroque old fish market at the foot of the Gravensteen, with a waterside terrace where the Leie and Lieve meet — classic dishes in one of Ghent's most scenic rooms.

dish: moderne fijnproeverskeuken — 2 Michelinsterren
w: Chef Michaël Vrijmoed's two-Michelin-star restaurant, Ghent's culinary summit — precise, produce-driven tasting menus with a celebrated cellar.

dish: groentegedreven menu — 1 Michelinster
w: Chef Olly Ceulenaere's one-star restaurant, quietly one of Belgium's most influential kitchens — a set surprise menu built around vegetables, ferments and Flemish produce.

dish: eigentijdse keuken met verrassende smaakcombinaties — 1 Michelinster
w: Chef Marcelo Ballardin's one-star OAK — contemporary, personal cooking with surprising combinations, on a quiet street near the Gravensteen.

dish: duurzame gastronomie — Michelin groene ster
w: Vilhjalmur Sigurdarson's intimate restaurant, holder of a Michelin Green Star for sustainable gastronomy — a tight seasonal menu rooted in Flemish and Nordic produce.

dish: verfijnd degustatiemenu — 1 Michelinster
w: A one-Michelin-star, small-room restaurant near the Kouter, praised for refined, well-balanced tasting menus and warm service.

dish: modern-Franse, farm-to-table keuken
w: A refined modern-French, farm-to-table table in Patershol, selected by the Michelin Guide — a small, chef-led room with a strong seasonal menu.

dish: moderne, creatieve Belgische keuken in Patershol
w: A Michelin-listed Patershol restaurant serving modern, creative Belgian cooking in a relaxed room — 3–4-course lunches, longer tasting menus at night.

dish: gastro-bistro — Gault&Millau Gastro-bistro van het jaar 2025
w: Chef Tom Pauweleyn's warm neighbourhood gastro-bistro, named Gault&Millau's Gastro-Bistro of the Year 2025 — creative, generous cooking off a lively square.

dish: idyllisch aan de Leie — Gault&Millau-adres
w: A long-loved Gault&Millau restaurant on the banks of the Leie south of the centre, with a waterside terrace — refined seasonal cooking away from the crowds.

dish: broodje Martino (pikante préparé) — dé Gentse uitvinding
w: The Ghent institution that claims to have invented the broodje Martino — spicy raw-beef préparé — still serving it, plus its famous cheese-egg-burger, in a no-frills snackbar since decades.

dish: veganistische burgers & dagschotels (veggiepionier sinds 1996)
w: Ghent's pioneering veg restaurant, open since 1996 and now fully vegan — burgers, bowls and daily specials that helped make the city Europe's self-styled veggie capital.

dish: plantaardige buddha bowls & whole-food sushi (bio)
w: An organic plant-based canteen — buddha bowls, whole-food sushi, tonic wines — small, warm and central; the Ghent original of a concept now exported worldwide.

dish: seizoensgebonden, lokale groentekeuken
w: A daylight bistro named for its ecological, local-produce philosophy — seasonal, largely vegetable-forward plates by the Glazen Straatje.

dish: vegetarische lunch met bio-ingrediënten bij het Gravensteen
w: A long-running vegetarian restaurant in a stepped-gable house opposite the Gravensteen, with a garden terrace — organic, seasonal lunches, a Ghent veggie fixture.

dish: grotendeels veganistisch lunchbuffet, wekelijks wisselend
w: A gentle lunch spot known for its generous, mostly-vegan buffet — spreads, salads and warm dishes that change with the season and the market.

dish: cuberdon / neuzeke — het paarse kegelsnoep (de 'neuzekesoorlog')
w: Two rival carts side by side on the Groentenmarkt sell Ghent's raspberry cone-sweets, the cuberdon or 'neuzeke' — a decades-long feud (the viral 'war of the noses') that has become city folklore.

dish: Gentse mostaard, vers uit het vat gepompt (sinds 1790)
w: A mustard shop unchanged since the 19th century, making Ghent's pungent mustard on the premises and scooping it, still fizzing, from a cellar barrel into stoneware pots before your eyes. Founded 1790.

dish: huisgemaakte cheesecake, taarten en gebak aan de Leie
w: A tiny, much-loved patisserie and breakfast spot on the Kraanlei overlooking the water — cheesecakes, pies and homemade granola in a doll's-house room.

dish: pralines met verrassende smaken (yuzu, tonka, truffel, peper)
w: Nicolas Vanaise's minimalist chocolate boutique, among Belgium's most admired — pralines built on unexpected flavours like yuzu, tonka, truffle and pepper. In the Gault&Millau chocolatier guide.

dish: ambachtelijke espresso — koffiebranderij sinds 1937
w: A cosy coffee roastery in the heart of Ghent since 1937 — dark, nostalgic and beloved by locals as much as visitors for a proper espresso.

dish: specialty coffee in een art-nouveaupand
w: A colourful 1904 Art Nouveau corner housing a welcoming specialty coffee bar and B&B on the edge of Patershol — organic, locally sourced, run by a British owner who fell for the city.

dish: cappuccino tussen exclusieve fietsen ('coffee with a side of cycle')
w: A coffee-and-bicycle bar near Portus Ganda where you sip a cappuccino among collectible bikes and gear — a cheerful spot on the water for cyclists and caffeine.

dish: specialty coffee & huisgemaakte appeltaart, bio brood
w: The Ghent bar of Belgian specialty roaster OR Coffee (founded here in 2009) — expertly pulled coffee, organic bread and cake, near the university quarter.

dish: koffie, aperitivo & tapas tussen de kunst
w: A coffee-and-art bar on the lively Kortrijksepoortstraat run by artist Dominique Ribas — coffee by day, aperitivo and tapas as the street's hip strip wakes up.

dish: ambachtelijk brood, grill & pizza uit een Scandinavische houtoven
w: Kobe Desramaults' bakery-restaurant — sourdough, wood-fired pizza and brunch from a Scandinavian oven — voted the country's best new concept when it opened and still a hotspot.

dish: verse frieten met veel veggie/vegan snacks (meermaals beste frituur van Gent)
w: A student-belt frituur repeatedly voted Ghent's best, famed for crisp fries and an unusually broad range of vegetarian and vegan snacks.

dish: frieten in plantaardige olie, ruim vegetarisch/vegan aanbod
w: A central frituur beside St Michael's, frying in vegetable oil with a wide vegetarian and vegan range — fries with a canal view.

dish: het 'julientje' — frietlegende aan de Overpoort
w: A near-legendary frituur at the top of student-nightlife street Overpoort, credited with inventing the 'julientje' — the late-night fix every Ghent student knows, meals under ten euros.

dish: ambachtelijke houtoven-pizza met Duvel-gistdeeg
w: A hip wood-fired pizzeria between the Gravensteen and the Groentenmarkt whose dough is raised with Duvel yeast — 'otomat' with red sauce, 'notomat' white; you can even moor a boat and order to the quay. In the Gault&Millau guide.

dish: creatieve seizoenskeuken in de Dampoortbuurt — Gault&Millau
w: A creative, seasonal neighbourhood restaurant near Dampoort with a Gault&Millau score — tight lunch and multi-course dinner menus in a warm room off the tourist track.

dish: koffie, huisgemaakte appeltaart en bio brood
w: A homely coffee-and-cake bar with organic artisan bread, art on the walls and a famous apple pie — a Ghent favourite for take-away or a slow morning by the Zuivelbrug.

dish: vegetarische burgers op meergranenbrood met zoete-aardappelfriet
w: A small order-at-the-counter veggie eatery a few blocks from the Gravensteen — multigrain veggie burgers, sweet-potato fries and thick shakes; a long-running Ghent meat-free staple.

dish: mastellen & worstenbrood uit Gents oudste bakkerij (sinds 1880)
w: Ghent's oldest bakery, baking in a 17th-century cellar workshop on the Groentenmarkt — tiny, nostalgic and known for mastellen and warm sausage rolls.

dish: Gentse streekbieren in een café-concertzaal bij Sint-Jacobs
w: A café, concert hall and gallery run by the non-profit that relaunched the Gentse Feesten in 1970 — beers, live music and a terrace on the Sint-Jacobs square, open every day.
